title: Extending Partial Orientations in Ancestral Graphs with Forest-Shaped Uncertainty and Background Knowledge
banked_reason: The advertised full-class contribution is not proved: EXTEND complexity remains open, while the sound forest-skeleton algorithm, local intersection closure, oracle self-reduction, and nonfactorization counterexamples form an incremental boundary result.
gap_reasons: The advertised full-class contribution—exact polynomial computation of K-essential endpoints and opposing witnesses when U(P) is a forest—is not proved; EXTEND complexity is explicitly left open.
The completion criterion is only a semantic verifier and supplies neither an efficient search procedure nor a hardness classification for the target class.
The framing is faithful about these limitations, but competent rewriting cannot turn the unresolved central extension problem into a field-level contribution.
proof_attempt_summary: The run attacked a polynomial sound-complete orientation and witness calculus for arbitrary ancestry knowledge on forest-uncertainty PAGs. It proved local intersection closure, a quadratic algorithm on the stricter forest-skeleton subclass, an oracle self-reduction, and explicit nonfactorization and endpoint-retention counterexamples. The full forest-U(P) EXTEND problem remained unresolved: no polynomial construction or canonical hardness classification was obtained, so the field-level promise collapsed to a sound incremental boundary.
tldr: For canonical selection-free PAGs with forest \(U(P)\), every local head relation is closed under finite nonempty intersections and contains the empty head pattern, but these relations do not factorize the represented MAG class.  A canonical six-vertex class of exactly twelve MAGs has locally realizable marks whose join creates a fixed-edge almost-directed cycle.  The generic four-condition completion test is only a verification specification.  The full-class question is now the complexity of partial-assignment extension: a polynomial extension algorithm would yield endpoint consensus and all opposing witnesses by self-reduction, but neither such an algorithm nor a hardness reduction is proved.  No polynomial finite-rule compilation is claimed.
gap: Exact incorporation of this ancestry language is known through global recursive completion, but no located result makes it polynomial on the forest-uncertainty subclass. Existing complete rule systems cover ordinary PAG information, tiered knowledge, or knowledge local to fully or specially resolved vertices; current edge-orientation work has different inputs and stronger structural hypotheses.
fill: Prove or refute the local-meet and gluing statements, compile the surviving structure into explicit finite polynomial rules, and accompany completeness by a constructive MAG certificate for each possible residual endpoint mark.
